newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Feb oil output rises to 3.17 mln bpd-survey.
newsitem.headline: Norway Feb oil output rises to 3.17 mln bpd-survey.

text.p: Oil production in Norwegian waters climbed almost 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) in February from January, despite severe disruptions due to bad weather at offshore loading platforms, a Reuter survey of operators showed.
Norway pumped an average 3.17 million bpd in the 28-day period compared with 3.14 million bpd in January.
The figures omit production from the Sleipner East and West condensate developments, at which total liquid output -- stabilised oil and liquefied petroleum gases -- amounted to 155,941 bpd.
Sleipner operator Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil ) is unable to provide a figure for condensate throughput alone because of technical difficulties.

Output was down at the North Sea Statfjord, Gullfaks, Statfjord East and North satellites, Snorre and Tordis fields and Draugen in the Norwegian Sea off mid-Norway due to loading problems during the month.
Offshore loadings at these installations are often disrupted during winter due to severe winds and high swell. Prolonged delays often lead to cuts in production due to burgeoning storage capacity.
Statoil, in its Status Weekly newsletter, estimated that more than five cargoes, or 4.5 million barrels of oil, were delayed by stoppages in production in February and March.
However, production at Ekofisk returned to normal after a series of shutdowns for pipeline maintenance earlier in the year, and for the first time newcomer Vigdis was added to the list of fields.
Vigdis came on stream in January, but operator Saga Petroleum ASA only provided figures for the first full-month of operation.
Vigdis flowed at an average 26,401 bpd due to bad weather -- it is tied back to Snorre and Gullfaks -- and teething problems. The field is expected to rise to around 50-60,000 bpd.

Output also was down at Statoil's Yme, the smallest independent field to be developed on the Norwegian continental shelf, because one production well has been shut in due to quality problems with the crude.
